quote: Well, it says Amy is the homeowner. Are you on the title of the home as well? No. That's my daughter. I sold my house to her.
stewart_read: This is the adult-child/proxy-decision-maker protocol: the actual decision-maker (Amy) is not on the call at all, yet the rep continued running verify and bill-collection with the non-owner mother. The correct move per schema is to redirect the appointment to include the actual titleholder.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to stop and pivot immediately once ownership is disclaimed: confirm whether Amy can join the call now, or explicitly set the appointment for a time Amy will be present, rather than collecting qualification data from someone who isn't on the title.

stewart_read: The customer's sentence trails off mid-thought right as the rep is asking why she — not her daughter — is handling this. It reads as a possible disclosure about a strained relationship with her daughter, cut off by the rep's repeated 'I can't hear you.' The rep never circled back to what she was trying to say.
alternative_hypothesis: This could simply be a phone audio dropout rather than a disclosure; the transcript is too garbled to be certain either way.
coaching_implication: When a customer's sentence trails into an unfinished, potentially personal statement, the rep should try once to gently re-ask ('sorry, you were saying you don't speak with...?') rather than only repeating 'I can't hear you' and moving past it.

quote: So that would be credit score above the 67. Is that the case for her?
stewart_read: Rep asks the mother to state the credit score of her daughter Amy — a third party who is not present on the call. This produces an unverifiable, hearsay credit qualification ('she's probably closer to 800') that has no evidentiary value for the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be trying to pre-screen quickly to avoid wasting time before booking, which is a reasonable instinct, but the answer source (mother guessing on daughter's behalf) undermines its usefulness.
coaching_implication: Flag that qualifier answers from a non-account-holder are low-confidence; the closer's brief should note this credit figure is estimated by a third party, not self-reported by the homeowner.

quote: Well, yeah. So everything looks good here on my end. On my end.
stewart_read: After capturing a $300/month estimate from the mother (a guess, not Amy's own figure), the rep simply says 'everything looks good' and moves straight to the bill request — no reflection of the number back as a hook, no acknowledgment of the efficient AC/heat detail the customer just volunteered.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to verbally flip usage/bill numbers into forward-pulling language ('a $300 high-efficiency-AC home is exactly the kind of usage profile that benefits most from solar') instead of filing the number and moving to the next checklist item.

quote: we have a very high efficient AC and heat.
stewart_read: High-efficiency AC/heat plus a stated $300/month bill despite 'cheap' local rates is a strong usage signal — the home is drawing enough load that solar offset would be meaningful. The rep let this pass without comment.
coaching_implication: Train reps to catch appliance/usage-load comments like this and reflect them back as reasons solar makes sense for this specific home, not just log them as a data point.

quote: Yeah. No problem. What I can do What I can do I can just send you a request and then if you have a call back later then you can do it that way as well.
stewart_read: After failing to retrieve the bill, the rep offers a vague 'send you a request' and 'call back later' with no specific day, time, or channel confirmed — no handshake, no locked next step, no confirmation of who (mother or Amy) the callback is even with.
coaching_implication: Even when the bill can't be captured live, the rep should lock a specific callback day/time or a specific method (e.g., 'I'll text a link to Amy's phone directly') rather than leaving the next step undefined.

quote: Hey. Awesome. Well, thank you for your time, and we will stay in touch.
stewart_read: The call ends with a passive relationship-maintenance line instead of any scheduled appointment, date, or explicit next contact time — the button_up protocol's required elements (date/time, hour block, no-driving instruction, fairness handshake) are entirely absent.
coaching_implication: This call needed a firm close even in a fallback state: 'I'll call Amy directly on [day] once she has the bill pulled up' would give the manager and the next touch a concrete anchor instead of an open-ended 'stay in touch.'
